summary: Service-mesh SSO claim trimming prevents new service accounts from accessing K8s dashboard and DB-provisioning console
description:
Issue summary:
Newly provisioned service accounts created via the service-mesh control plane intermittently receive an SSO assertion where certain claims (notably 'aud' and a custom 'roles' array) are being trimmed/truncated by the mesh gateway. When the trimmed assertion is consumed by internal RBAC services, token validation succeeds but role assignment fails, producing 403s for the K8s dashboard and the internal DB-provisioning console.

Impact:
- Several infra automation jobs and platform engineers reported failing access to the k8s dashboard and the DB-provisioning UI after creating service accounts through the mesh.
- Affected flows are limited to newly issued service-account assertions (existing sessions remain valid).
- Estimated ~12 teams impacted across infra and platform in us-west.

Environment:
- Prod cluster behind service-mesh gateway (env: prod/us-west).
- Mesh control plane version: meshctl v2.7.1.
- SSO provider: Okta (SAML->OIDC bridge in the mesh).
- RBAC enforcement: internal auth-service v3.4.0 using 'roles' claim mapped from SSO assertion.

Steps to reproduce:
1) In prod-us-west, create a new service account via meshctl (provisioning path used by platform-automation).
2) Trigger the onboarding job which requests an SSO assertion for the new account.
3) Attempt to access Kubernetes dashboard as that service account or use the DB-provisioning console.
4) Observe RBAC denying access with 403 and symptoms in auth-service logs.

Observed logs / errors:
- auth-service: "RBAC: role mapping missing for subject=sa-mesh-20260312 org=infra"
- mesh-gateway (ingress): "Assertion sanitized: dropped claim 'roles' length=0 -> trimmed"
- Okta assertion logs (SAML bridge): shows full 'roles' present upstream; trimmed state appears after mesh gateway step.

Workaround applied:
- Platform SRE temporarily bypassed the mesh gateway for the provisioning callback path (route flagged to passthrough SSO headers) which restored correct claims and allowed affected service accounts to access the dashboard and console.

Desired end state:
- Fix in mesh gateway to preserve custom SSO claims (roles, aud) for service-account assertions and deploy a patch to prod-us-west.
- Add automated integration test for SSO claim preservation in the mesh provisioning flow.
comments: Support (2026-03-12): Triage - beginning investigation with SRE and mesh team. Slack thread #platform-auth: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CPLATFORMAUTH/p1612345678000

SRE - Alejandro (2026-03-12): Applied temporary passthrough route to provisioning callback to unblock teams; monitoring for side effects. Recorded change in runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/sso-provisioning-passthrough

Platform Eng - Priya (2026-03-13): Confirmed Okta assertions upstream include 'roles' and 'aud'. Observed trimming in mesh-gateway container logs. Added initial hypothesis that an L7 policy sanitizes header payloads over size threshold.

Mesh Team - Lukas (2026-03-13): Reproduced locally with meshctl v2.7.1 and saw claim trimming when header length > 8kb. Filed GH issue and starting patch: https://github.com/redwood/mesh-gateway/pull/492
SRE (2026-03-14): Will schedule a targeted canary deploy of the mesh-gateway patch to prod-us-west tonight in a staged rollout and monitor auth-service metrics and 403 rate.
investigation_notes: 01 - Reproduced the failure by creating new SA and capturing traffic between mesh-gateway and auth-service; observed header truncation at mesh-gateway egress.

02 - Confirmed Okta SAML->OIDC bridge emits full roles claim in JSON assertion; mesh-gateway configured with an L7 policy that rewrites headers to a custom 'x-ss-assertion' value which truncates long payloads.
03 - Hypothesis: Mesh gateway rewrites and stores assertion in a cookie/header which has a length limit and internal trimming logic introduced in v2.6.9. Regression introduced in PR #447.
04 - Mitigated by passthrough route; verified auth-service received full claim and RBAC mapping succeeded for test accounts.
05 - Risk assessment: patching mesh-gateway is low risk if canaried; but global config changes to header size caps could impact other large-claim assertions (SAML groups arrays).
resolution_notes: Mitigation: passthrough route created to bypass mesh-gateway assertion rewrite for provisioning callback (applied 2026-03-12).
Planned fix: mesh-gateway patch merged PR #492 to preserve claim payloads; canary rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 23:00 UTC to prod-us-west.
Follow-up: add regression test in mesh-gateway CI to reject PRs that shrink/strip SSO claims; update runbook to document claim-size limits.
